correctness.rationale: Five folded-cube Cayley generators have only the all-ones binary relation. Every closed five-step walk uses each once; so 16*5! graph-Hom vertices. All one-cell recolorings are adjacent transpositions of two generator steps, commuting precisely for two nonadjacent source-cycle positions. This yields a 2-dimensional cubical cell complex with 1920 vertices, 4800 edges and 2400 squares. Each vertex link is a five-cycle and each edge has two squares; connectivity follows from adjacent transpositions and weight-two translations, and coherent orientations from permutation parity. Hence a closed connected orientable surface of Euler characteristic -480, genus 241. Integral homology and orientation group character follow. verify.py performs two vertex enumerations, exhaustive cellular incidence and local-link checks, a signed fundamental 2-cycle construction and all 1920 affine orientation actions.

value.rationale: The five-regular Clebsch graph is a canonical (16,5,0,2) 4-chromatic triangle-free strongly regular graph that lies exactly outside recent square-free-target Hom classifications. The fact that its pentagon Hom complex is a connected orientable surface of genus 241, rather than a union of points and circles, is a nontrivial global classification with explicit structural mechanism (cyclic adjacent generator swaps) and a nontrivial sign orientation character under affine symmetry. These precise invariants are natural to the graph coloring/homotopy construction and not simple restatements of a previously cited theorem. The claim is intentionally target-specific; no general arbitrary-graph significance is asserted.
